channel.title: Twinthos Notes
channel.description: An evidence-led publication about intelligent systems and their consequences. Original investigations, independent model tests, and sourced analysis, organised into six desks.

item.title: What an AI agent actually does when you give it a computer
item.description: Browser tools, file systems, calendars. The vendor demos show agents finishing tasks in minutes. The independent research is more cautious, and more useful.

item.title: What the public AI benchmarks actually measure, and what they don't
item.description: MMLU, GPQA, SWE-bench, AIME, LMArena. Every lab cites them. Each one has a narrow test set, a known failure mode, and a year-old headline number. A reading guide.

item.title: Why AI automations fail after the demo
item.description: A working demo takes an afternoon. A working production workflow takes a year. The independent research on why the gap is so wide, and what closes it.

item.title: The real cost of running an AI employee vs hiring one, in 2026 numbers
item.description: A worked example with public list prices, published wages, and the four assumptions that change the answer. The cost is rarely the headline number.

item.title: Bank tellers were supposed to disappear with the ATM. They didn't.
item.description: Half a century of US Bureau of Labor Statistics data, and a research result that complicates the obvious forecast. What it says about new technology and the people who use it.
